theme: The pierced one; the Day of the LORD; living waters
readingInstruction: Read Zechariah 12:1-14:21. The LORD defends Jerusalem, a mourning comes over the house of David, a fountain opens for sin, a shepherd is struck, and the LORD becomes king over all the earth. Read 12:10, 13:1, and 14:9 with care.
settingTheScene: This is the second oracle, and it is the most apocalyptic section of the book. It uses vivid, symbolic language to describe the end: a siege of Jerusalem, a great mourning, a day of cleansing, and the final victory of the LORD. The New Testament draws heavily on it, especially in the stories of Jesus’ death and in Revelation.
observation: “And I will pour out on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and pleas for mercy” (12:10).
“When they look on me, on him whom they have pierced, they shall mourn for him, as one mourns for an only child” (12:10).
“On that day there shall be a fountain opened for the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and uncleanness” (13:1).
“Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered” (13:7).
“And I will put this third into the fire, and refine them as one refines silver” (13:9).
“They will call upon my name, and I will answer them. I will say, They are my people; and they will say, The LORD is my God” (13:9).
“On that day his feet shall stand on the Mount of Olives” (14:4).
“And the LORD will be king over all the earth. On that day the LORD will be one and his name one” (14:9).
interpretation:
Chapter 12 begins with a statement of God’s power: he stretched out the heavens and founded the earth. Then he promises that Jerusalem will become a cup of staggering and a heavy stone for all the peoples who attack her. God defends his people. But the real victory is spiritual. Verse 10 is among the most important verses in the Old Testament: God will pour out “a spirit of grace and pleas for mercy,” and the people “will look on me, on him whom they have pierced.” God himself speaks, and the pierced one is both God and someone else. The result is great mourning, like the mourning for an only child. It is repentance, a result of grace.

Chapter 13 gives the cleansing. “A fountain opened… to cleanse them from sin and uncleanness.” It is the answer to the problem the whole Old Testament has been dealing with. Sin cannot be washed away by ritual. A fountain must be opened. Idols and false prophets will be removed.

Then comes the haunting verse 7: “Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.” The shepherd is “my companion,” says the LORD. God commands the striking of the one who is close to him. This is the suffering shepherd of chapter 11. Through it, one third will be refined as silver and gold, and will say, “The LORD is my God.”

Chapter 14 takes us to the end: the nations fight against Jerusalem, the LORD goes out to fight, his feet stand on the Mount of Olives, which splits in two. Living waters flow out from Jerusalem. Darkness and cold are no more. “And the LORD will be king over all the earth.” Even the pots in Jerusalem will be “holy to the LORD.” The book ends with everything, even the common cooking pots, marked as holy. All of life is consecrated.
connection: John 19:34-37 says that after the soldiers pierced Jesus’ side, “They will look on him whom they have pierced,” quoting Zechariah 12:10. Revelation 1:7: “Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, even those who pierced him.” Matthew 26:31 quotes “I will strike the shepherd.” 1 John 1:7: the blood of Jesus cleanses us from all sin. Acts 1:11-12: Jesus ascends from the Mount of Olives. Revelation 22:1: the river of the water of life.
application:
Read John 19:31-37 and look at the pierced one.

Thank God for the fountain opened for sin, and take your own sin there.

Ask God to make “everything holy,” even the ordinary pots of your life: your kitchen, your work, your errands.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to pour out a spirit of grace and pleas for mercy on you.
Look on the one who was pierced, and tell him what you see.
Thank him for the fountain that cleanses sin.
